reconcile.connective: Defenders answer that Gad's territory was Amorite land Sihon had seized from Ammon, so Israel never touched Ammon's own possession that Deuteronomy protected.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells presses that the standing command to leave Ammon undisturbed cannot be squared with Jephthah's slaughter of Ammon and Yahweh's oracle that Rabbah be burned to a desolate heap.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013)

excerpts.excerpt_text: but then that was what Sihon king of the Amorites had taken from them, and which Israel retook from him, and so possessed it not as the land of the Ammonites, but of the Amorites, one of the seven nations, whose land they were to inherit …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly resolves the protection-clause tension: the only Ammonite-adjacent land Israel held (Gad's) was Amorite land Sihon had taken from Ammon and Israel won from the Amorites, not Ammon's own possession Deut 2:19 protected.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Deuteronomy 2:19
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, arguing the land Israel held by Ammon was Amorite territory Sihon had seized, never Ammon's protected possession.
